inference.at_its_ceiling: Three rounds is the ceiling. A fourth parks this claim, keeping what it found.

claim: The delay a type prints `FL Dly` against and the loop it prints `FL Fb` against are, in both types that print them inside a larger chain, the delay and the loop of the stereo flanger that stands alone. Read as a comb at two settings of the delay byte and on both signs of the loop, all four readings of each type return the single type's figures exactly: 0.618 ms at a delay byte of 6 and 1.318 ms at 13 with the loop in phase, 0.624 and 1.296 with it inverted. That holds where the chorus runs into the flanger and where it sits beside it, so neither arrangement carries a delay line of its own. The teeth are 22.58 dB deep at the shallowest against the 16.05 dB the deepest of these records asks of one, and each profile scores as a comb of that spacing by at least 1.55 times what the same profile scores read on the other sign -- which is the control a filter sitting somewhere cannot imitate, since a peak scores the same either way. The modulator behind that delay is the single type's too, on the type the chorus runs into it. Its rate byte returns a table over ten settings whose four published ones are the single flanger's to four figures -- 1.6499 against 1.65, 4.9994 against 4.9993, 6.1007 against 6.0974, 9.9991 against 9.9986 Hz -- and the settings between them fall on the same line. Its depth byte buys the single flanger's excursion at every setting either run reads, to within 1.71 per cent against the 0.42 per cent one setting taken twice repeats to. On the type the chorus sits beside, the modulator is not read here: the reading that returns a rate picks a period out of an autocorrelation, and on that type the frequency series of a partial stands taller at twice the rate than at it at most settings of the flanger's feedback byte and carries nothing at the rate at all at the centre of it, which is where every run that is not asking about the loop parks that byte.
adds: The single type's claim says the byte is a loop and says what it is around. It says that on one type. These two print the same pair of bytes at the same addresses over the same printed ranges, and nothing structural had been read on either of them -- the only claims naming them were the two that run across every type, about what a parameter powers up holding and about what happens to a byte its page prints no state for. What is added is that the stage a combination names after another type is that type's stage, read on the one quantity a delay line cannot fake: where its comb sits.

values.why: A modulation the tracker cannot recover from a take it was put into by hand is not evidence that the unit applied none, and nothing in the output separates the two. So every run puts a known modulation into one of its own takes and reports which depths came back. It bounds the run in both directions and neither alone: a null is worth reading only over the depths the control recovered, and a rate found at a depth shallower than the shallowest of those is a fit the tracker was never shown able to make on this material.

document_rows.why: The two combinations print a delay and a feedback over the same ranges the stereo flanger prints them over, at the same pair of addresses. That is what made the question worth asking and it is not what answers it: a page printing two ranges alike is a page, and the comb is the unit.

era_priors.claim: A combination effect of this period is built from the same blocks the single effects are, because the blocks are code and memory that already exist and a second copy of a delay line costs both.
era_priors.why: Carried, not closing. The same prior would have been offered for the bass multi-effect's amp table, and that one reaches a table of its own -- so this is a reason to ask rather than an answer.
era_priors.would_be_wrong_if: Either combination's comb had sat at a spacing of its own. It is wrong somewhere on this unit already: the bass multi-effect's amp entries sit a median 7.7 dB from the same entries read anywhere else, which is wider than that table's own entries are from each other. So the prior is a reason to ask and the comb is what answers.

alternatives.reading: Each combination carries a delay line of its own, tuned to the same printed range.
alternatives.ruled_out_by: Two separately built delays would have to agree with the single type's and with each other at both settings, and the reading resolves them finely enough for that to be a claim: the fit returns 0.618 ms against 1.318 for a delay byte moving from 6 to 13, which is a ratio of 2.133 where the byte's own is 2.167. All eight readings across the two types land on the single type's two figures and on no other.

alternatives.reading: The teeth are a filter of the combination's own rather than a loop, and they happen to sit where the single type's do.
alternatives.ruled_out_by: A comb and a peak are told apart by what happens below the printed nought of the feedback byte. Every profile was scored both as an in-phase comb and as an inverting one, and each of the eight scores at least 1.55 times better on the sign its setting implies -- the settings under the centre on the inverting reading and those over it on the in-phase one. A filter sitting somewhere scores the same both ways.

alternatives.reading: The chorus in front of or beside the flanger is still in the path, and what was read is the two stages together.
alternatives.ruled_out_by: Each run wrote the chorus out of the path in the way its own arrangement allows -- the series type's chorus balance to its dry end, the parallel type's chorus level to nothing -- and parked its rate and depth as well. A modulated stage left in the path smears a comb into a shelf, which is what the first published reading of a modulated type came back as; these come back as combs of a single spacing.

alternatives.reading: The two combinations share one delay line with each other but not with the single type.
alternatives.ruled_out_by: They return the single type's figures, not a third pair. There is nothing left for this reading to be about.

alternatives.reading: The half named inside `11 02` agrees on where the comb sits and differs somewhere -- in the balance or in the output stage. The modulator is answered on both combinations, though not by the three coming out identical: read at the feedback byte all three types power up holding, the excursion the depth byte buys differs between them by a fraction of what a different modulator was measured to cost on this machine, so a second modulator is refused and a trimmed one is not.

separated_by.observable: The pitch excursion each type's depth byte buys, read the way the single types' were, and the balance byte's two ends.

predicts.one stage throughout: the combination's depth byte buys the single flanger's excursion at every setting
predicts.the same delay under a different modulat: the excursions differ by more than either repeats to

separated_by.sensitivity_here: The single types' depth runs repeat to 2.74 per cent and the flanger and the chorus differ there by a ratio from 1.316 to 1.501, so the reading separates two modulators by two orders of magnitude more than it repeats to. The rate the two sides are read at has to be established from the height of the frequency series at a named frequency rather than from the period a picker returns: the two differ by an octave on this type.
separated_by.why_not_separable: The two branches left are not the modulator's, and neither is reachable by a reading this archive publishes. Where a balance byte puts the two paths equal is a property of the mixture and no stage here publishes one, so a difference found between the three types by sweeping that byte cannot be cited however many times it is taken. The lag between the unit's two outputs is in the same position: it is a quantity the takes carry and nothing publishes. What is missing on both is a stage rather than a booking, and the takes both questions need are recorded.

refuted_by: A comb in either combination that sits at a spacing the single type does not return, at either delay setting or on either sign of the loop. One reading off the single type's two figures by more than the width the fit reports would say the stage is named after something it is not.
what_it_would_change: Rendering either type needs one delay line and one loop, with the milliseconds the single type's table gives, rather than a second table read off these types. Thirty of this unit's sixty-five types are combinations named after others, and this is the second stage to be asked whether the name reaches the block -- after an equaliser section, and with the same answer.
what_this_does_not_settle: What the rest of either type is. Two bytes of twelve and of fourteen carry a reading here; the chorus halves, the balances, the pans and the output levels carry none.

Whether the delay is one block reached from three places or three copies of one design. Nothing measurable from outside separates a shared block from identical copies, and this claim says the stage behaves alike and not where it lives.

how_each_type_was_put_into_its_flanger.arrangement: a chorus running into a flanger
how_each_type_was_put_into_its_flanger.why: A comb read through another stage's output is a comb around something else, so the chorus is put out of the path rather than left where the type powers it up. The series type's chorus has a balance and no level, so it goes to its dry end and passes its input through; the parallel type's has a level, so it goes to nothing. Both have their rate and depth parked as well.

why_this_is_not_a_round_of_the_single_ty: The claim it tests has had three rounds, which is where this project parks one so that a single type cannot absorb the work. And what is claimed here is about two other types: a finding about `02 0B` and `11 02` filed under a file named after `01 23` is a finding nobody looking for those two would find.
the_reading_was_corrected_before_this_wa: The bar a tooth has to clear is three times the spread across the run's own repeats of one setting, which is the record's own `floor_db`. It was being taken from the bypass control instead. The two are the same size on the single type -- 3.14 dB against 1.37 -- and they are not on a type whose effect-alone path sits far from its dry one, where the control stands 20.38 dB off while the repeats stand 3.71, and teeth 26 dB deep were being refused by it. A bar that tightens as the effect gets louder is backwards. The correction moved nothing the single type's claim quotes: it returns the same two delays, and two settings it had refused now read and return them as well.

the_round_that_read_the_modulators.what_was_asked: Whether the modulator driving each combination's flanger delay is the single type's, which is the half of round one's standing alternative a rate and a depth can reach.
the_round_that_read_the_modulators.what_came_back_on_the_series_type: The rate table over ten settings, monotonic from 0.4482 Hz at a byte of 8 to 9.9991 at 127, with four partials of four agreeing at eight of the ten. The four settings the single flanger's table is published at agree to four figures. The depth byte buys the single flanger's excursion at every setting either run reads.
the_round_that_read_the_modulators.what_came_back_on_the_parallel_type: Nothing this claim can carry. A run of this project read the same slot of that type at twice the published figures at every setting both types carry, and the published record of the slot -- taken with nothing else written -- returns the single flanger's figures with four partials of four agreeing. Both cannot be readings of one thing.
the_round_that_read_the_modulators.why_the_doubled_reading_was_not_publishe: It was bisected to one byte and then to the reading. Adding each part of the held block to the bare type one at a time doubled nothing; leaving each part out of the whole block returned the single flanger's line only when the flanger's feedback byte was the part left out. Swept across that byte the slot returns four values and no others -- a third of the single type's figure, a half of it, it, and twice it -- which is a period picker landing on a multiple rather than a rate moving. What decides between them is not the period but the height of the frequency series at each of those four named frequencies, taken over the roughness beside each rather than over the whole band's median. On the parallel type the fundamental stands out of that roughness at 11 of the 12 settings and the second harmonic is the taller of the two at 9; on the series type the fundamental stands at all 12 and is the taller at 11. Half the rate is the null -- a modulator running at a rate puts no line there -- and across both types it comes back between 0.8 and 2.5 times its own roughness.
the_round_that_read_the_modulators.why_two_readings_agreeing_was_not_a_chec: The level of a partial and its instantaneous frequency are two quantities, and they agreed on the doubled figure on both channels of the interface. They are not two readings: both are handed to one period picker, so a multiple that wins for one wins for the other. A reading is corroborated by a second reading and not by a second input to the first.
the_round_that_read_the_modulators.the_one_setting_where_the_fundamental_is: The centre of the feedback byte, which is no loop. At that one setting the parallel type's fundamental stands 1.1 times its roughness, inside the range the null occupies, where the lowest of the other 11 stands 6.8. No bar decides this: the one that fails is below the next by a factor of six, so anything between the null and that figure counts the same eleven. The series type's fundamental stands 108.1 at the same setting, so this is the parallel arrangement's and not the byte's.
the_round_that_read_the_modulators.why_that_setting_is_the_one_every_other_: It is the printed centre, so every run of this type that is not asking about the loop parks the byte there -- including the sweep of the rate byte. Read in that arrangement the slot returns twice the single flanger's figure at every setting of the rate byte and carries nothing at the figure itself, which reads like a modulator running at twice the rate. It is not one. A modulator's rate cannot follow a byte inside the delay's loop, and eleven settings of that byte put the fundamental back. What the centre does is make the output even about the middle of the sweep: with no loop the comb has one notch, it crosses a partial going up and again coming down, and both series repeat at half the period without the modulator changing. The frequency series does not break that tie either, which was the reading this round expected to -- the pull on a partial follows where the notch sits relative to it, not which way the sweep is going.
the_round_that_read_the_modulators.the_counts_this_replaces: This round first reported the fundamental present at all twelve settings, the second harmonic tallest at eleven, and the series type's fundamental tallest at ten. Re-read they are 11, 9 and 11. The first is the one that mattered: a count that says the fundamental is always there hides the single setting where it is not, and that setting is the one the rest of this type's runs are taken in. The conclusion the round drew is unchanged and rests better on the corrected numbers than on its own.

why_the_standing_alternative_carries_no_: The model is unchanged. What this recorded is that one of the two readings this archive has into a modulator's depth does not reach one of the types, and that the other fails its own null there -- which moves a queue entry and revises nothing the claim states. A count of rounds that went up for it would spend the last revision this claim is allowed on bookkeeping, and would say the model had been taken further than it has.

the_round_that_closed_the_modulator.what_was_asked: Whether the modulator driving the parallel combination's flanger delay is the single type's, which round two could not reach and recorded as an obstruction in the type.
the_round_that_closed_the_modulator.why_it_was_reachable_after_all: The obstruction was a setting and not a type. Round two's note says a partial on the parallel arrangement is a sum of paths and its frequency is not the frequency of the modulated one, which is true -- and it is true at one setting of one byte nobody had moved. Every depth run in this archive was made with the flanger's feedback byte at 64, and the page prints that byte as `-98% - +80% - +98%` over hex `0F - 71`, which puts nought per cent at 64 rather than at the middle of a byte. So every earlier run of all three types was made with the loop open, and an open loop is the one arrangement in which the comb has a single notch and the sweep is symmetric about its own turnaround. The power-on value of that byte is 104, which is `+80%` and which all three types share, so moving the reading was not necessary: moving the setting to the one the unit itself loads was enough, and at 104 every type returns the commanded rate on the fundamental.
the_round_that_closed_the_modulator.a_record_it_rests_on_was_re_read: The parallel combination's two depth records were read from the quieter of the unit's two outputs, and the figures above are what they give read from the other one. The two types this round compares it against print Low Gain and Hi Gain at `40 03 13` and `40 03 14`; on the parallel type those addresses are Cho Level and FL Pan, so the run that silenced the chorus at the first of them panned the flanger hard to one side at the second, and the stage then picked the side it was not on -- by a fifth of a decibel, off the control take where the two outputs are equal by construction. Across all eighteen swept takes the output that was read sits 22 dB under the other and at the level of an input nothing is plugged into. The records named every one of those takes as loudest elsewhere, which is the archive saying so; what was missing was a reading of it. Re-read, the five takes at the compared setting scatter over 2.1 per cent where they scattered over 9.4, and this round's figures moved with them: the difference between the three types is larger than it was and the margin over what a different modulator costs is about half what it was. It still closes the branch, and it closes it by less.
the_round_that_closed_the_modulator.what_came_back: At the depth the three runs share, the excursion off the phase averaged over five takes is 01 23 9.8845 ms, 02 0B 10.6943 ms, 11 02 11.5826 ms -- a spread of 1.6981 ms, 15.8 per cent of their own mean. The five-take range at the same setting is 01 23 4.9 per cent, 02 0B 5.7 per cent, 11 02 2.1 per cent. As ranges no two of the three meet -- 01 23 9.6244 to 10.1092; 02 0B 10.4391 to 11.0444; 11 02 11.4666 to 11.7151 ms -- so every difference reported below is larger than the scatter either side of it was measured over.
the_round_that_closed_the_modulator.how_far_apart_the_three_are: As means they do not overlap. 01 23 against 02 0B 0.8098 ms, 6.1 times the error on those means; 01 23 against 11 02 1.6981 ms, 18.7 times the error on those means; 02 0B against 11 02 0.8883 ms, 7.6 times the error on those means. The widest of the three, 01 23 against 11 02, is 15.8 per cent of the pair's own size. A difference between the types is therefore present in this reading, and what the round says about it is how large it is and not that it is absent.
the_round_that_closed_the_modulator.what_closes_the_branch: Not that the three agree, and they do not. Five takes of one setting on each type sit further apart between the types than they scatter inside one, so a difference between the types is present in this reading and is reported rather than smoothed away -- where the three ranges fall against each other is above. What closes the branch is the size of it. The branch asks whether the flanger inside the combination is driven by a different modulator, and round one measured what a different modulator costs on this machine: the single flanger and the chorus that shares its front end differ across the depth byte by a third to a half. The difference found here is a fraction of that, and the run was shown able to see the larger one before it was asked for the smaller. A second modulator is refused; the same modulator trimmed is not, and that is a different sentence.
the_round_that_closed_the_modulator.what_it_does_not_close: That the three modulators are identical, which this run does not say and is not asked to. The excursions differ by more than the error on the means they are measured as, so something between the three types is not the same. It is too small to be a different modulator by the only measurement this archive has of what one costs, and every remaining reading of it -- a trim in the depth table, a difference in the balance the two paths are summed at, a gain ahead of the delay -- is in the branches the alternative already carries and is not separated here.
the_round_that_closed_the_modulator.which_floor_is_the_gate: The floor this is measured against is the one at the setting the comparison is made at, and not the loosest proportion the run produced anywhere. Whether those are the same thing is not assumed: the same five takes were made at two depths whose excursions differ several-fold, so the run says for itself whether repeats hold to a fixed number of milliseconds or to a fixed proportion of what the setting buys. Both floors are reported below with what the figures make of them, because a fixed-size floor quoted as the proportion it becomes at the smallest setting in the sweep is a fact about the sweep rather than about whether two types can be told apart where they were compared.
the_round_that_closed_the_modulator.how_the_floor_behaves: Whether five takes of one setting repeat to a fixed number of milliseconds or to a fixed proportion of what the setting buys, asked of each type on its own: 01 23 excursions spanning 3.09 to one against a five-take range spanning 1.06 to one; 02 0B excursions spanning 3.23 to one against a five-take range spanning 3.52 to one; 11 02 excursions spanning 2.17 to one against a five-take range spanning 1.31 to one. The three do not read the same way, so this run does not settle which it is, and the gate is taken at the compared setting for both readings rather than argued from one of them. Read at the setting the comparison is made at the worst range is 5.7 per cent; the loosest proportion anywhere in these runs is 14.3 per cent, and that one is substantially the same milliseconds divided by a smaller excursion.
the_round_that_closed_the_modulator.the_discriminator_it_was_measured_agains: A different modulator shows as a ratio of 1.316 to 1.501, which is 32 to 50 per cent. The difference this run found between the three types is 15.8 per cent, and the smallest a different modulator has been measured to cost is 1.99 times that. At the compared setting the worst of the three five-take ranges is 5.7 per cent, so the difference a different modulator makes is 5.58 times that range and this run could have seen one.
